reason: I need a case to hold and protect the core, so folding the metal seems like a sensible first step.
expectation: I expect the jig to form a case shell, though it may need insulation and cooling afterward.

alternatives.reason: The packs will be needed to keep it cold, but I want the container first.

effect: The jig produced the shell as expected; I can now insulate it.
reason: Insulation belongs in the shell to slow warming of the sample.
expectation: I expect an insulated case, still needing refrigeration.

alternatives.reason: Freezing the packs is also useful, but I want to finish the case structure first.

effect: The shell is now insulated, leaving the cooling insert to fit.
reaction: It behaved as expected; nothing surprising.
reason: The refrigeration insert should actively keep the insulated case cold.
expectation: I expect a refrigerated field case; the packs may still be needed as backup.

alternatives.reason: The packs need freezing too, but I am continuing the case assembly.

effect: The case now has refrigeration; the remaining offered action is preparing the packs.
reaction: The assembly is logical but predictable so far.
reason: Freezing the packs is the only offered combination and should prepare extra cooling.
expectation: I expect cold packs ready to install in the case.

effect: The packs are charged and the text clarifies that they buffer incoming heat only temporarily and need refrigeration to recharge.
reaction: I liked the distinction between passive heat absorption and active cooling; it gives the packs a clear purpose.
reason: The only offered combination puts the charged packs with the refrigerated case for transport.
expectation: I expect a completed cold case with the packs as a temporary buffer.

effect: The packs complete the buffered case, so it is ready for the intended core collection.
reaction: It is satisfying to have assembled the case, though the final result is terse.

mostWorthwhile.text: Charging the packs explained their limited heat-absorbing capacity and the role of active refrigeration; that made the design clearer.

leastWorthwhile.text: The shell and insulation steps were sensible but predictable, with little detail beyond the created objects.

surprise.text: I had not considered that active refrigeration must restore the packs' capacity after they absorb heat.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the assembly sequence was clear, though the later choices were forced.

continue.text: Yes. I want to see whether the protected ice contains a whole ridged object, although this case-building sequence itself offered little decision-making.
